mil5.2.7:0.4: 7. Question on Looking After the Community of Bhikkhus
mil5.2.7:1.1: “Venerable Nāgasena, this too was said by the Blessed One:
mil5.2.7:1.2: ‘Ānanda, it does not occur to the Tathāgata, “I will look after the community of bhikkhus,” or “The community of bhikkhus is under my direction.”’
mil5.2.7:1.3: Yet in describing the natural qualities of the Blessed One Metteyya, the Blessed One also said:
mil5.2.7:1.4: ‘He will look after a community of many thousands of bhikkhus, just as I now look after a community of many hundreds of bhikkhus.’
mil5.2.7:1.5: If, Venerable Nāgasena, the Blessed One said
mil5.2.7:1.6: ‘It does not occur to the Tathāgata, “I will look after the community of bhikkhus,” or “The community of bhikkhus is under my direction,”’ then the statement ‘I now look after a community of many hundreds of bhikkhus’ is false.
mil5.2.7:1.8: ‘He will look after a community of many thousands of bhikkhus, just as I now look after a community of many hundreds of bhikkhus,’ then the statement ‘It does not occur to the Tathāgata...’ is also false. This too is a two-horned dilemma that has come to you; you must resolve it.”
mil5.2.7:2.1: “Your majesty, the Blessed One did say ‘Ānanda, it does not occur to the Tathāgata, “I will look after the community of bhikkhus,” or “The community of bhikkhus is under my direction.”’
mil5.2.7:2.2: And he also said, in describing the natural qualities of the Blessed One Metteyya:
mil5.2.7:2.3: ‘He will look after a community of many thousands of bhikkhus, just as I now look after a community of many hundreds of bhikkhus.’
mil5.2.7:2.4: In this question, your majesty, one meaning has an exception and one meaning has none.
mil5.2.7:2.5: The Tathāgata, your majesty, does not follow the assembly; rather the assembly follows the Tathāgata.
mil5.2.7:2.6: ‘I’ and ‘mine’ are, your majesty, conventional usage; they are not the ultimate truth. Affection has gone from the Tathāgata, your majesty, and attachment has gone. There is no grasping in the Tathāgata even at ‘this is mine’; there is only a support that depends on a basis.
mil5.2.7:3.1: Just as, your majesty, the earth is the foundation and support of beings living on the ground, and those beings rest on the earth, yet the great earth has no concern that ‘these are mine’;
mil5.2.7:3.2: in just the same way, your majesty, the Tathāgata is the foundation and support of all beings, and those beings rest on the Tathāgata, yet the Tathāgata has no concern that ‘these are mine.’
mil5.2.7:3.3: Or again, your majesty, when a very great rain cloud pours down, it gives growth to grass, trees, animals and humans, and sustains their continuity.
mil5.2.7:3.4: All those beings live dependent on the rain, yet the great cloud has no concern that ‘these are mine.’
mil5.2.7:3.5: In just the same way, your majesty, the Tathāgata generates and sustains wholesome states in all beings; all those beings live dependent on the Teacher, yet the Tathāgata has no concern that ‘these are mine.’
mil5.2.7:3.7: Because the view of self has been abandoned.”
mil5.2.7:4.1: “Well said, Venerable Nāgasena. The question has been thoroughly untangled by many kinds of reasoning; what was profound has been made plain, the knot has been broken, what was dense has been made open, darkness has been made light, the doctrines of opponents have been shattered, and an eye has been produced for the sons of the Conqueror.”
